diagram.title: Reference architecture
diagram.hint: Follow the path of a request and select each component.

client.label: Clients
client.text: Web (Next.js with SSR/ISR) and mobile apps consuming a versioned contract, OpenAPI or GraphQL. Contract tests and backward compatibility let client and server deploy independently.

gateway.label: Access
gateway.text: Entry point with OAuth2/OIDC, JWT validation, rate limiting and abuse protection. Coarse-grained authorization is enforced at the edge and domain-level authorization inside each service, with least privilege.

services.label: Services
services.text: Hexagonal architecture in NestJS: use cases and ports in the domain, adapters for persistence and messaging. Bounded contexts with DDD, dependency inversion, and domain tests that need no running infrastructure.

events.label: Events
events.text: Asynchronous communication between contexts with idempotent producers, the outbox pattern, exponential-backoff retries, dead-letter queues and circuit breakers that contain a failing dependency.

data.label: Data
data.text: Persistence chosen by access pattern: PostgreSQL as the transactional source with indexes, partitioning and versioned migrations; Redis for caching; MongoDB for documents. Point-in-time recovery backups with tested restores.

ai.label: AI
ai.text: RAG pipeline: document ingestion and chunking, embeddings, semantic search over a vector database, input and output guardrails, and continuous evaluation of relevance and faithfulness to sources before changes ship.

platform.label: Platform
platform.text: Infrastructure as code with Terraform, minimal container images, and deployment on ECS, Lambda or Kubernetes. Pipelines run SAST, dependency and image scanning, and block promotion to production on vulnerabilities.

observability.label: Observability
observability.text: Correlated metrics, logs and traces with OpenTelemetry. SLOs are defined with product, and alerts fire on user impact rather than infrastructure noise.

capabilities.title: Capabilities
capabilities.subtitle: Five areas where I can support your team. Pick one to see what I deliver and how I approach it.

items.title: Backend architecture and APIs
items.summary: Services your team can understand, test and grow without rewriting them.
deliver: REST and GraphQL APIs with versioned contracts (OpenAPI) and contract tests
Modular NestJS or FastAPI services with hexagonal architecture, and DDD where the domain warrants it
Relational and NoSQL modeling, indexes, versioned migrations and a caching strategy
Event-driven processing with idempotency, retries, DLQs and circuit breakers
approach: I separate domain, use cases and infrastructure with OOP and SOLID so logic can be tested without spinning up infrastructure
I agree on the contract with its consumers before writing code
I record every significant decision as an ADR, with alternatives and consequences

items.title: Generative AI and RAG in production
items.summary: AI features with measurable quality, controlled costs and explicit limits.
deliver: Ingestion, embedding and semantic search pipelines over vector databases
RAG flows and agents with LangChain, LangGraph or Semantic Kernel
Input and output guardrails, plus automated evaluations of relevance and faithfulness to sources
Tracking of cost per query, latency and answer quality (LLMOps)
approach: I define the use case and the success metric before choosing the model
I keep a human in the loop where risk demands it and protect sensitive data before it reaches a model
I evaluate every prompt, model or data change before release and monitor it in production

items.title: Cloud, platform and reliability
items.summary: Reproducible infrastructure, frequent releases and operations you can measure.
deliver: Infrastructure as code with Terraform on AWS (ECS, Lambda, SQS/SNS) and Azure
CI/CD pipelines in GitLab or GitHub Actions with per-environment deployments and rollback
Containers with Docker, and Kubernetes when the case justifies it
Observability with Grafana, CloudWatch or DataDog: metrics, traces, alerts and SLOs
approach: Every infrastructure change goes through code, review and a pipeline
I define SLOs with product and alert on user impact, not noise
I review cost from the design stage (FinOps) so the platform scales without surprises

items.title: Security and DevSecOps
items.summary: Security built into the design and the pipeline, not bolted on at the end.
deliver: Authentication and authorization with OAuth2/OIDC, JWT and Auth0, using roles and least-privilege permissions
Pipelines that block deployments with vulnerabilities: static analysis (SAST), dependency and image scanning
Secrets management, encryption in transit and at rest, and API hardening aligned with OWASP API Security
Threat modeling and architecture review for systems that handle sensitive data
approach: I apply least privilege to users, services and pipelines
I automate controls so they run on every change, not only during audits
I translate risks into business impact to prioritize what to fix first

items.title: Technical leadership and business alignment
items.summary: Technical decisions explained in business terms, and teams moving in the same direction.
deliver: Technical discovery: scope, risks, dependencies and assumptions in writing
Proposals with alternatives, cost and trade-offs, ready for a decision
Staged delivery plans with priorities agreed with product
Code review, quality guidelines and mentoring for the team
approach: I translate business requirements into measurable scope and explicit risks
I present options with their impact instead of a single answer
I facilitate agreements between product, engineering and operations, and document the decision

process.title: How I work
process.subtitle: A short, transparent process that scales to the size of the challenge.

steps.title: Discovery
steps.text: I understand the context, constraints and what success means. I leave with scope, risks and assumptions in writing.

steps.title: Design
steps.text: I propose an architecture with alternatives and trade-offs. We decide together and the decision is recorded.

steps.title: Incremental delivery
steps.text: I ship in stages, with tests and pipelines from the first one. Every release can be demonstrated and rolled back.

steps.title: Operation and handover
steps.text: I leave observability, documentation and practices your team can sustain without depending on me.

about.title: About David Zapeta
about.lead: Backend, cloud and generative AI engineer based in Mexico City. I design and operate the platforms behind real products.
story: I started in 2018 in digital banking, optimizing queries, data models, and backup and recovery processes. That is where I learned that a reliable system depends on well-modeled data and disciplined operations.

I then moved into full-stack and backend development with a DevOps mindset: REST and GraphQL APIs, React and Vue interfaces, GitLab CI/CD pipelines and resilience patterns such as DLQs and circuit breakers.
Today I design microservices in NestJS and FastAPI, infrastructure with Terraform on AWS and Azure, and generative AI features built on RAG, guardrails and observability.

principles.title: Design is decided with the team
principles.text: I present alternatives with their trade-offs and document the decision, so it can be reviewed and improved.

principles.title: Security is not a phase
principles.text: Controls live in the design and in the pipeline, and run on every change.

principles.title: What you don't measure, you can't operate
principles.text: I decide which signals matter before instrumenting, and alert on user impact.

principles.title: The system belongs to the team
principles.text: I leave documentation, tests and practices behind so nobody depends on a single person.
